label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hi everybody, it's Hélène from Pétrin Doré. My nephew showed me this thread this morning so yes, Mr. Bergeron, I read it, and you are right, people deserve a straight answer. So here it is, a little earlier than I planned.

**We are not closing. We are not moving. We bought the building.**

I wanted to keep this for the reopening, I had a whole little speech ready, but I think the surprise is finished now. That's ok. I'd rather you know the truth than worry for one more week.

So, from the beginning.

**About the building**

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right. The building at the corner was sold. It was sold to me! We signed at the notary on December 15th.

Most of you know M. Ferland, the owner. He is 81 now and he is retiring to Sherbrooke to be near his daughter. When he decided to sell, he came to me first, before anybody else, before any agent or developer. He said he wanted the bakery to stay. For 17 years he came every single morning for his baguette, pas trop cuite, always the same, and I think for him it was important that this corner stays the same too. He cried a little at the notary. Me too, a little, I admit.

So no condos, no bank, no vape shop. Just bread, like always.

**The upstairs tenants**

If you live in one of the three apartments upstairs and you read this board, please don't worry. Nothing changes for you. Same apartment, same rent. I already promised it to each of you in writing, and I will keep my promise. You are my neighbours first, and I'm not going to start being a landlord by making people nervous about their home.

**Why we close January 4 to 18**

We are doing works. Two big things:

First, the oven. My old deck oven is from 1998 and it broke three times this year. Some of you were there the morning in the spring when there was no pain de campagne until almost noon, so you know. A new 4-deck oven is coming from a supplier in Laval, and it needs to be installed properly, and that takes time. With the new oven, more bread, more regular, and I hope less days where I'm on the phone with the repair man at 5 in the morning.

Second, the space at the back. You know the old storage room from the dépanneur behind us? Now that I own the building, we can finally use it. We are opening it up and putting in 6 small tables. After all these years of people eating their croissant standing on the sidewalk in February, you will finally be able to sit down. I'm very happy about this one.

**We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7h in the morning.** Same hours as before after that.

**About the sign**

Ok, I have to confess something. The sign on the door was written by my nephew Thomas, at 6 in the morning, while I was busy with the ovens. "Grande nouvelle bientôt!" was his idea. He thought it was exciting. I said ok without really thinking about it. I see now how it looks, a vague sign plus a closed bakery plus rumours about the building. It looks bad, I understand. Thomas feels terrible, and I told him it's not his fault, it's mine, I'm the boss. Next time I will write the sign myself, and with more words.

**About the empty shelves on the 28th**

That was Christmas! We sold everything for Christmas Eve. 400 bûches this year, a record for us. After that there was nothing left on the shelves and honestly there was nothing left of me either. Nothing to do with closing. It was just the best December we ever had, thanks to you.

**Now, the carnets**

This is the part I want to be very clear about.

In October we sold 214 carnets, $60 for 12 loaves. **Every carnet is still good. There is no expiry date. There was never an expiry date.** If you have 7 loaves left, you have 7 loaves left, in January, in June, in 2030, whenever you want.

And to say thank you for your patience during the closing, every carnet holder gets a free croissant when you come in January. Just show your carnet.

And if somebody really wants their money back for what's left on their carnet, you can. Come see me at the counter, and I give it back. No question, no explanation needed. I mean that.

I'll be honest, the word "scam" hurt me. I've been on this street since March 2009. 17 years of getting up at 3h30, of knowing your kids' names, of saving the last pain aux olives for the people I know are coming at 6pm. I'm not saying this to make anybody feel bad. I understand why people worry. Mile End lost a lot of small shops in the last years, places we all loved, and very often it started exactly like this, a sign on the door and then nothing. So I understand the fear. I just want you to know it's not that, and it was never that.

Mr. Bergeron, thank you for asking directly and politely. It was the right question and you deserved the answer.

**Thank you**

Priya, thank you for defending us, it really touched me. And your little one is still welcome for his chocolatine on Saturdays, the new oven makes no difference for that. Thank you also to everybody who sent me messages or stopped Thomas on the street to ask if we were ok. To jules_on_waverly, don't worry, the pain de campagne is not going anywhere. If anything there will be more of it.

**You're all invited, Saturday January 23**

To celebrate properly, I want to invite everybody to the bakery on **Saturday, January 23**. Free coffee and a piece of the first bread from the new oven, for everyone. Regulars, new people, people who thought we were closing, people who called us a scam, everybody. Come try the new tables, see the back room, and tell me if the bread is as good as before. You're always honest with me, so I count on you for that too!

I'm also going to ask M. Ferland to come down from Sherbrooke if he can. I will have a baguette pas trop cuite ready for him.

So that's the whole story. Not the surprise I planned, but maybe it's better like this.

See you on the 19th at 7h, and on the 23rd for the coffee.

Hélène
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré, Fairmount

P.S. Thomas wants me to say that he still thinks "grande nouvelle" was the right words, because it IS big news. He's not completely wrong.
